marking_points.point: A proxy server improves data security and network performance by acting as a firewall and web filter, providing shared connections, and caching data.
marking_points.quote: Proxy servers act as a firewall and web filter, provide shared network connections, and cache data to speed up common requests.

marking_points.point: Network segmentation protects the network by placing boundaries between segments whose computing assets share a common function, risk or role.
marking_points.quote: Boundaries between network segments where computing assets within the segment have a common function, risk or role within an organization.

marking_points.point: A remote access VPN protects the network by giving individual hosts or clients remote and secure access to the organization's network.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access protects the network by ensuring a user only has the access and permission required to fulfill the role.
marking_points.quote: A user should only has access and permission that required to fulfill the role

marking_points.point: Intrusion detection and prevention systems protect the network by detecting or preventing attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.
marking_points.quote: To detect or prevent the network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Explain how a rail fence transposition cipher encrypts and decrypts a message.

marking_points.point: Encryption writes the plaintext in a zigzag across rows and then reads letters row by row to form the ciphertext.
marking_points.quote: The plain-text is written in a zigzag pattern in rows and form the cipher-text by reading off the letters from the rows.

marking_points.point: The key is a positive integer giving the number of rows used in the rail fence.
marking_points.quote: The key for a rail fence cipher is a positive integer that represents the size of rows.

questions.question: Describe six points about biometric mechanisms and technologies, covering their definition, categories, and the advantages and disadvantages of specific biometric methods.

marking_points.point: A biometric is defined as a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another and can theoretically be used for identification or verification of identity.
marking_points.quote: A biometric is a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another and that theoretically can be used for identification or verification of identity.

marking_points.point: Biometric applications are categorized into two sectors: psychological (physiological) and behavioural.
marking_points.quote: Biometric applications available today are categorized into 2 sectors

marking_points.point: The psychological (physiological) category includes iris, fingerprints, hand, retinal and face recognition.
marking_points.quote: Psychological: Iris, Fingerprints, Hand, Retinal and Face recognition

marking_points.point: The behavioural category includes voice, typing pattern and signature.
marking_points.quote: Behavioural: Voice, Typing pattern, Signature

questions.question: List two formal security models and state the concern each addresses.

marking_points.point: The Bell-La Padula (BLP) model is a formal security model that deals with access control only.
marking_points.quote: Bell-La Padula (BLP) model: access control only

marking_points.point: The Chinese Wall model is a formal security model aimed at identifying conflicts of interest.
marking_points.quote: Chinese Wall model: identification of                                                                 conflicts of interest

questions.question: Explain THREE (3) components of the NGSCB architecture and the role each plays in establishing a trusted platform.

marking_points.point: The Nexus is a security kernel that is authenticated during boot and authenticates trusted programs.
marking_points.quote: Security kernel, authenticated on boot

marking_points.point: The Nexus provides the application interface to the TPM and does not trust the operating system.
marking_points.quote: Application interface to TPM

marking_points.point: The Nexus Computing Agent is a trusted software component that runs in trusted mode and communicates with the Nexus.
marking_points.quote: Runs in trusted mode that communicates with Nexus

marking_points.point: The Nexus is a special kernel at the core of the trusted operating environment whose goal is to isolate normal-mode and trusted-mode processes differently in memory.
marking_points.quote: Goal:  Isolate the process of  normal mode and                                                  trusted mode                                                                                differently in memory

marking_points.point: The Nexus authenticates and protects data that is entered, stored, communicated and displayed by means of data encryption.
marking_points.quote: Functionality: Authenticate and protect data                                                    (entered, stored, communicated, and                                                             displayed) by data encryption

marking_points.point: The TPM is a tamper-resistant hardware module mounted in the platform that is responsible for measurement, protected storage, integrity reporting and policy enforcement.
marking_points.quote: Trusted Platform Module (TPM): a tamper-resistant hardware module mounted in a platform.

questions.question: Discuss six malware attack techniques and propagation methods described in the lecture, explaining how each technique operates or spreads.

marking_points.point: Rootkits hide malicious processes and software so that the attacker keeps privileged remote access to the infected system.
marking_points.quote: Rootkits are a type of malware that mask malicious processes and software in the infected systems to ensure privileged remote access.

marking_points.point: Spyware spies on users by stealing logins and passwords, recording visited sites, logging keystrokes and redirecting browsers.
marking_points.quote: They steal user logins and passwords, document sites visited, log keystrokes and even redirect browsers to unwanted sites.

marking_points.point: An executable virus can append its virus body to a host program so that the malicious code is carried along with it.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program

marking_points.point: An executable virus can overwrite a program header to switch the entry point to the virus, then jump back to the original entry point during execution.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: The Morris worm used a debugging feature of sendmail for remote execution and propagated across the Arpanet, penetrating about 6,000 computers.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution)

marking_points.point: The Brain virus spread in the wild by being included in the boot sector of distributed software diskettes.
marking_points.quote: Included in a boot sector of distributed software diskettes

questions.question: State six points about the Samy worm and XSS attacks as described in the lecture, covering how the worm spread, how XSS is delivered, and why XSS is possible.

marking_points.point: The Samy worm injected JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: The worm obtained the list of a user's heroes by performing a GET on the user profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: The worm added Samy as a friend by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any user visiting an infected user's page had their profile and friends list infected, and about 1,000,000 MySpace profiles were eventually infected.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: In the XSS example, the attacker inserts a malicious string into the website's database using one of its forms, and the victim's browser later executes the malicious script, sending the victim's cookies to the attacker's server.
marking_points.quote: The attacker uses one of the website's forms  to insert a malicious                                                                                                               string into the website's database.

marking_points.point: Any web application that returns user input without filtering is a potential XSS vulnerability, allowing execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the user's browser.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

questions.question: Describe six Windows security mechanisms and features, including how subjects and access rights are handled and how the platform's complexity affects security.

marking_points.point: Windows includes complex mechanisms for managing user accounts, objects and access control.
marking_points.quote: Windows systems contain complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.

marking_points.point: Discretionary access control enables fine-grained control over diverse entities in Windows and its applications.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.point: The complexity of these mechanisms can itself cause severe security incidents through misconfiguration or implementation bugs.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

marking_points.point: Windows treats processes and threads as the active subjects in the operating system.
marking_points.quote: Windows subjects are processes and threads.

marking_points.point: Security credentials for a subject are kept in a token that maps principals to subjects and is inherited when new processes are created.
marking_points.quote: Tokens provide a principal/subject mapping and may contain additional security attributes.

marking_points.point: Access rights are encoded as a 32-bit mask and include standard rights such as the ability to change an object's DACL or owner.
marking_points.quote: WRITE_DAC: change object’s DACL

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Explain six ways the ACM code guides a computing professional's conduct and ethical practice.

marking_points.point: The professional should aim for high quality in the processes and products of their professional work.
marking_points.quote: Strive to achieve high quality in both the processes and products of professional work.

marking_points.point: The professional should uphold strong standards of competence, conduct and ethical practice.
marking_points.quote: Maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice.

marking_points.point: The professional should be aware of and respect the rules that apply to their professional work.
marking_points.quote: Know and respect existing rules pertaining to professional work.

marking_points.point: The professional should give and receive suitable professional review.
marking_points.quote: Accept and provide appropriate professional review.

marking_points.point: The professional should contribute to society and human well-being, recognising all people as stakeholders in computing.
marking_points.quote: Contribute to society and to human well-being, acknowledging that all people are stakeholders in computing.

marking_points.point: The professional should act honestly and be trustworthy.
marking_points.quote: Be honest and trustworthy.

last_draft.scenario: A medium-sized organisation is deploying a single sign-on (SSO) solution based on Kerberos across its distributed network of servers and clients.

questions.question: Explain five characteristics of Kerberos as a single sign-on mechanism that the organisation should consider when deploying it across its distributed network.

marking_points.point: Kerberos is designed to prevent eavesdropping by ensuring that passwords are never transmitted in clear text.
marking_points.quote: Security against eavesdropping: no                                       password transmission in clear text.

marking_points.point: Kerberos is transparent to users because they are unaware of any authentication beyond the initial login.
marking_points.quote: Transparency: user is not aware of any                            authentication beyond an initial login.

marking_points.point: Kerberos scales to support a large number of servers and clients.
marking_points.quote: Scalability: support for a large number of                                          servers and clients.

marking_points.point: Kerberos provides secure authentication even over an insecure network.
marking_points.quote: Provides secure authentication in an                                     insecure network.

marking_points.point: Kerberos suffers from a single point of failure, which is a drawback for the deployment.
marking_points.quote: Single point of failure.
